Sasha: heads-up — after the 1765 runtime kernel swap + tokenizer v2.4 rollout we’re seeing a large warmup miss delta on KV cache for chat routes, ~20% miss vs ~5% baseline :eyes:
Miguel: got a chart? rough numbers?
Sasha: yes, quick dump from the perf dashboard:
```
route: /v1/chat.generate
period: 10m
hits: 83k
misses: 20.6k
hit_rate: 80.2% (was 95.4% before)
median_warmup_latency: 48ms -> 120ms
```
Dan: oof. did anything else change at the same time? tokenizer changes, or key serialization?
Sasha: two things: kernel swap (prefetch ordering changed), tokenizer export switched to v2.4 (normalization differences), and we flipped a tool-field encode flag to include function metadata in probe keys.
Priya: likely causes: 1) tokenizer produces different token boundaries -> different probe prefixes 2) extra tool metadata in key -> exploding namespace 3) kernel prefetch ordering created eviction pressure at warmup due to different batch ordering.
Alice: I profiled a sample of misses vs hits. Misses have much higher entropy in the first 8 tokens. example:
```
input A (hit): "Summarize: \"Q...\"" -> token prefix: [105, 8, 23, 2, 301]
input B (miss): "Summarize: \"Q...\"" (same text) -> token prefix: [105, 8, 24, 2, 301]  // one token diff from tokenizer v2.3->v2.4
```
Alice: that single-token drift cascades into different kv-key fingerprint for probe prefix.
Miguel: so small tokenization shifts are mapping identical user-visible strings to different cache bins. Can we canonicalize on normalized text (NFKC + whitespace trim) before tokenizing?
Dan: canonicalization helps but will not solve function/tool fields being included. Which code path appends tool meta?
Sasha: runtime/transport -> probe_key() — we recently toggled include_tool_meta=true to help reranking feature rollout.
Priya: for short-term mitigation I propose:
- roll include_tool_meta=false for warmup-sensitive routes (chat.generate, chat.stream)
- add a token-version header to keys so we can segregate v2.3 vs v2.4 and run TTL backfill analysis
- introduce a tiny canonicalizer for common divergences (smart quotes, trailing spaces, repeated newlines) before tokenization
Miguel: +1. Also add a bandaid: a small LRU boost for prefix cache on nodes that did kernel switch to reduce eviction while we stabilize. cheap and reversible.
Alice: I measured foldback rate after kernel swap: eviction rate for warm prefixes increased by 2.8x in the first 2 minutes after deploy. That aligns with prefetch ordering change where long-tail low-utility batches were being prefetched earlier.
Dan: can we change prefetch ordering policy to favor short-seq, high-frequency prefixes during warmup window?
Sasha: yes — runtime has a bias flag. I'll push a canary that flips prefetch_bias=hot_first on one ASG. deploy-bot: canary queued (canary-asg-7)
perf-bot: profiler snapshot 1765432410 uploaded: /perf/1765432410/prefix-entropy-profile.csv
Miguel: good. we also need to audit any probe-key fields that are non-stable: toolcall order, function arg dict ordering, and system prompt timestamps. Those are easiest to normalize at probe construction.
Priya: agreed. plan of action:
1) revert include_tool_meta on prod-critical routes (Sasha)
2) enable prefetch_bias=hot_first canary (Sasha)
3) add token-version tag in probe key + start collecting cohorts (Alice)
4) implement canonicalizer + deterministic field ordering for tool metadata (Dan/PR)
5) run a background rewarm job for top-10k prefixes sampled from last 24h (Miguel)
Sasha: timeline?
Miguel: revert + canary within 30m. cohort tagging + telemetry update by EOD. canonicalizer PR tomorrow. rewarm job in 48h.
Alice: one more note — we should avoid a global rollout of tokenizer v2.4 until the canonicalizer is in. Otherwise we’ll keep oscillating hit-rate as we flip nodes.
Dan: will open a quick RFC for deterministic tool metadata ordering and include examples.
Priya: can we also add an experiment to compute "warmup entropy" (Shannon) for prefixes and auto-tag noisy prefixes so they get a special caching policy?
Miguel: nice idea. auto-tagging noisy prefixes to a separate bucket with longer TTL could help. add to backlog as a follow-up experiment.
Sasha: thanks team. I'll start the revert and canary and post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
Miguel: thanks — keep notes of any regressions from the canary.
Sasha: update: canary went out, initial hit_rate on canary nodes moved from 81% -> 92% in 12m. will wait 30m for steady state.
Alice: saved profiler snapshot for pre/post canary. linking in case someone wants raw samples.
perf-bot: snapshot links: pre: /perf/1765432100/prefix-sample.pbz, post: /perf/1765432460/prefix-sample.pbz
Dan: awesome. next steps after stabilization: formalize probe key spec in docs and add unit tests to prevent regressions.
Sasha: agreed. closing loop when back to baseline.
